context.strategy:
# Strategy

## Goals — Current focus (next 4-8 weeks)
- Hold a 3-run + 2-lift rhythm in weeks that allow it, ~15 km running
- Build tempo capacity: extend tempo segments toward 3 km @ sub-5:10/km
- Sleep tracking compliance above 70%
- VO2max above 46

## Goals — Medium-term (3-6 months)
- Sub-25 min 5K — the pre-COVID PR, needs roughly 5:00/km sustained
- VO2max above 47
- Consistent 4-run weeks when the schedule allows

## Goals — Ongoing
- Build and maintain a strong, lean physique — progress compound lifts while
  staying injury-free
- Family and health always take priority over numbers

## Weekly Shape

There is no fixed weekly schedule and there should not be one. Work and family
decide how many sessions a week contains. This section decides what to do with
however many there are.

**Week runs Monday → Sunday.** Prefer weekday mornings; keep weekends free for
family. Prefer not to stack a run and a strength session on the same day.

When the week is short, build up from the top and stop where it runs out:

1. One easy run
2. One strength session (alternate Push and Pull week to week)
3. A second easy run
4. The second strength session
5. Tempo work inside one of those runs

A five-session week is 3 runs + 2 lifts with tempo in one of them. A two-session
week is one easy run and one strength session — and that is a complete week for
that week, not a failed one.

**Tempo is the first thing to drop, not the last.** It is the highest-value
session when everything else is already in place, and the worst one to force
into a compressed or under-recovered week. Run it when recovery is at or above
recent normal — use the computed baselines rather than a fixed number.

**Nothing carries over.** A session missed this week is not owed next week.
Never plan a catch-up week, and never escalate a target because something was
skipped.

## Adapting week to week

- Recovery below normal, or short sleep: keep the session, drop the intensity.
  An easy run beats a skipped one.
- Office-heavy or travel week: expect a compressed week and shape it on Monday
  rather than reacting on Friday.
- Two consecutive weeks at two sessions or fewer: revisit the goals above. That
  is a signal the targets no longer fit the season, not a reason to demand more.
- Tempo skipped three weeks running while easy runs continue: ask whether the
  sub-5:10 target still matches current volume.

## Strength sessions

- Strength A: Push + core (DB bench press, OHP, dips; progressive overload)
- Strength B: Pull + core (pull-ups, rows, deadlift; progressive overload)

## Runs

- Easy pace 5:30–6:00/km, around 5 km
- Tempo, when it happens: segments of 1.5–2.5 km at 5:05–5:15/km
- Rest days: walking, optional core/mobility, usually active with son

## Diet

Pescatarian. Target 120g+ protein (~1.5 g/kg). No strict calorie tracking.

## Sleep

Target 7+ hours, realistically variable with a young child.
Track sleep at least 5 of 7 nights per week.

## 2026-W28

- Visible priority: next week is recovery-focused, easy running only, lifts only if recovery allows.
- Open thread: easy runs are costing more heart rate than they should; if that does not ease it points to deeper aerobic fatigue.

## 2026-W29

- Visible priority: recovery compliance, not volume, is the measure of next week.
- Open thread: easy-run heart rate still has not come down, and it gates the return of any intensity.

## 2026-W30

- Easy-run heart rate came back down, clearing the gate that had been blocking intensity.
- Open thread: recovery swings continue, so intensity stays conditional on them settling.

## 2026-W31

- Open thread: easy-run heart rate has returned to mid-July levels; keep monitoring whether it comes down when the remaining runs are genuinely easy.

## 2026-W32

- Visible priority: keep the 3-run rhythm with easy running prioritized; do not extend tempo beyond 2 km unless recovery is at recent normal, and skip intensity rather than forcing it.
- Open thread: improved overnight recovery has not yet translated into relaxed running; monitor running strain next week.

## 2026-W33

- Visible priority: consolidation week—keep sessions easy and drop tempo unless recovery returns to recent normal; do not add volume.
- The current recovery strain looks more like a training-load/recovery mismatch than an obvious sleep shortage.

## 2026-W34

- Visible priority: keep next week easy; tempo remains conditional on recovery returning to recent normal.

## 2026-W35

- Friday’s long hike with substantial climbing plus a lift preceded the higher-cost Sunday run; late-week load looks to be affecting running cost despite normal weekly totals.

## 2026-W36

- Visible priority: make tempo the next upgrade, only when that day’s recovery is at recent normal; otherwise keep the run easy without chasing volume.
- Open thread: running cost remains inconsistent between otherwise similar runs; monitor whether it settles when recovery is normal.

## 2026-W37

- Visible priority: keep next week easy; do not add volume or force tempo until recovery returns to recent normal.
